name: Filee
works_with: Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13 or newer (preview), Linux x64 and ARM64
short: Converts files between 255 formats offline: hold a key, drag files and drop them on a format that pops up at your cursor.
what: Filee is a file converter you use by dragging. Hold Ctrl (Option on a Mac), drag files, and a donut of formats opens at your cursor. Drop them on one and the result is saved next to the original. It handles images, PDFs, Office files, HWP, e-books, archives, fonts, CAD and 3D files without Office or LibreOffice. A `filee` command does the same from a terminal.
who: Anyone who converts files often and doesn't want to upload them to a website. Mac users should know the macOS version is a preview.
needs: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 13 or newer, or Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) with Python 3
On Linux, X11 for drag gestures. On Wayland, use the drop zone and the right-click menu
Video, audio and some document formats need an optional engine (FFmpeg, LibreOffice, Pandoc, calibre or Ghostscript), which Filee downloads when needed

steps.title: Download it
steps.text: Get the package for your system from the latest release on GitHub.

steps.title: Install on Windows
steps.text: Run `Filee-<version>-win-Setup.exe`, or unzip the `win-Portable.zip` and run `Filee.exe`. Setup can add the Explorer menu, the `filee` command and optional engines.

steps.title: Install on a Mac
steps.text: Unpack the `osx-arm64` or `osx-x64` package and run `./install.sh`, or open the `.dmg` and drag Filee to Applications. Only `install.sh` adds the `filee` command.

steps.title: Install on Linux
steps.text: Unpack the package and run `./install.sh`. It needs no root.

steps.title: Convert something
steps.text: Hold Ctrl (Option on a Mac), drag files and drop them on a format. Press Tab or turn the mouse wheel to flip the donut to less common formats.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Convert a folder of PNGs to WebP at quality 80: `filee convert *.png --to webp --quality 80 -o converted`.

watch: The macOS build isn't notarized, so allow the first start in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Open Anyway.
Windows releases are signed, but SmartScreen can still warn about a new release. Choose More info, then Run anyway.
Files never leave your computer. Filee checks GitHub for updates every few hours, which you can turn off in Settings, About.
Links dragged from a browser are downloaded without your browser's sign-in.
On an old, unpatched Windows 10 PC, Filee may not start at all. Install Windows updates first. The README has a PowerShell fix if you can't.
